sentences.text: This synthetic document describes the Cr–Fe binary system as calculated with pycalphad from the SGTE dataset CrFe-11Xio.tdb; every figure, table and stated value is generated, and the exact values are kept in a separate truth key.
The highest invariant reaction, σ → (Cr,Fe)1 + (Cr,Fe)2, lies at 790 K.
The Cr–Fe system belongs to the 20 binaries of the ORCHID benchmark, chosen to cover diagram types such as intermetallic, gamma loop, solid miscibility gap.

The thermodynamic description is the SGTE collection entry [1], which reproduces the assessment of W. Xiong, P. Hedstrom, M. Selleby, J. Odqvist, M. Thuvander, Q. Chen, Calphad, 35, 355-66(2011). [2].
The calculations use pycalphad 0.11.2 at 1 atm.
Eutectoid equilibrium σ → (Cr,Fe)1 + (Cr,Fe)2 is found at 790 K and 50.8 at.% (σ).
According to Table 2, σ remains stable up to 1086 K (congruent transformation).
At 2250 K the integral mixing enthalpy of the liquid has its maximum, 37 J/mol, at 78.0 at.% Fe.
The calculated enthalpy of formation of σ at 298.15 K is 5.89 kJ/mol per mole of atoms.
Its heat capacity at room temperature is 24.12 J/(mol K).
For the equiatomic liquid at 2250 K, the Gibbs energy of mixing is −16.33 kJ/mol.
This document is synthetic and exists only to test extraction tools; its truth key lists every boundary, field, invariant, plotted point, table cell and stated value.
